title: Lead Engineer Got an Offer
description: Your lead engineer just got a job offer from a competitor. They want a 30% raise to stay.

choices.label: Counter-offer with 30% raise
choices.outcome_text: They accept. Morale stabilizes but your burn rate just went up.

choices.label: Let them go
choices.outcome_text: They leave. The team is shaken and productivity drops while you backfill.

choices.label: Counter with equity instead
choices.outcome_text: They accept the equity deal. They're more invested now — literally.

title: Cloud Costs Doubled
description: An unoptimized database query has been running in production for weeks. Your cloud bill doubled this quarter.

choices.label: Pull an engineer to fix it now
choices.outcome_text: Fixed. But that engineer's feature work is delayed.

choices.label: Pay the bill and move on
choices.outcome_text: Expensive lesson. At least nothing else broke.

title: Viral TikTok Moment
description: Someone posted a TikTok about your product and it's blowing up. +50K signups in 48 hours. Can your infrastructure handle it?

choices.label: Scale up infrastructure immediately
choices.outcome_text: Servers held. You captured the wave. Users are flooding in.

choices.label: Hope for the best
choices.outcome_text: Site went down for 3 hours during peak traffic. You got some users but lost more.

title: Team Conflict
description: Two team members are clashing over technical direction. It's dragging down the whole team's morale.

choices.label: Mediate the conflict yourself
choices.outcome_text: Took a full day but they found common ground. Team respects you stepped in.

choices.label: Side with the senior engineer
choices.outcome_text: Right technical call, but the other engineer feels unheard. Watch that morale.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.outcome_text: It festers. Two weeks later the junior puts in their notice.

title: Security Vulnerability Disclosed
description: A user found a security vulnerability and posted it on Twitter. The clock is ticking.

choices.label: All-hands emergency patch
choices.outcome_text: Patched in 6 hours. Transparent incident report earns respect.

choices.label: Patch quietly over the weekend
choices.outcome_text: Fixed, but people noticed the silence. Trust took a hit.

title: VC Wants Coffee
description: A partner at a well-known VC firm reached out for a casual coffee chat. Could lead to a funding round.

choices.label: Take the meeting
choices.outcome_text: Great conversation. They want to see your metrics next quarter.

choices.label: Not ready yet — decline politely
choices.outcome_text: They respect the focus. Door stays open for later.

title: Competitor Goes Free
description: Your biggest competitor just raised $50M and is offering their product for free. Users are comparing you.

choices.label: Launch a free tier to compete
choices.outcome_text: You stem the bleeding. Free users are pouring in, but conversion is uncertain.

choices.label: Double down on quality and stay premium
choices.outcome_text: You lose some price-sensitive users but your paying customers are more loyal.

choices.label: Slash prices 50%
choices.outcome_text: Keeps you competitive but your margins just got a lot thinner.

title: Surprise Weekend Refactor
description: A junior developer you hired 3 quarters ago just mass-refactored the codebase over the weekend. Code is cleaner but untested.

choices.label: Review and keep the changes
choices.outcome_text: Impressive initiative. Tech debt way down, but a few bugs slipped through.

choices.label: Revert everything
choices.outcome_text: Safe call, but the junior is deflated. Others wonder if initiative gets punished here.

title: Acquisition Offer
description: A larger company wants to acquire you. The offer is decent but you're just getting started.

choices.label: Accept the offer
choices.outcome_text: You sell. The team gets payouts. The dream continues under a bigger roof.

choices.label: Decline and keep building
choices.outcome_text: The team is fired up. Turning down money to bet on yourselves — that's startup energy.

title: Bad Glassdoor Review
description: A former employee rated your company 2/5 stars on Glassdoor. 'No work-life balance, founder is clueless.' Ouch.

choices.label: Respond publicly and professionally
choices.outcome_text: Mature response. Candidates notice you handle criticism well.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.outcome_text: It lingers. Your next three candidates all mention they saw it.
